text:
The famous ship that sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg is the **RMS Titanic**.

To help you understand the concept of **Blockchain technology** using an analogy, imagine a **shared Google Doc** that everyone in a large organization can view, but only one person can edit at a time, and every change is permanently recorded with a timestamp and the editor's name.

Here is how the analogy maps to the technical details:

1.  **Digital Ledger**: Think of the Google Doc as the ledger. It contains all the transactions (changes made to the document).
2.  **Decentralized**: Instead of this document being stored on one company’s server (a central authority), imagine that every employee in the company has their own exact copy of this document on their personal computer. This is like the "thousand different computers" mentioned in your text.
3.  **Immutable**: Once a line is written in this special document, it cannot be erased or altered. If you make a mistake, you have to add a new line correcting it, but the old line remains visible forever. This makes the history permanent and unchangeable.
4.  **Verified and Agreed Upon**: If someone tries to secretly change their copy of the document to say they have more money in the bank (for example), the other 999 copies will not match. The system automatically compares all copies. Since the majority (the other 999 computers) disagree with the single altered copy, the change is rejected. This ensures that only valid, agreed-upon changes are accepted, making the system extremely secure and trustworthy.

In short, blockchain is like a public notebook that everyone has a copy of, where no one can erase or rewrite past entries, and any new entry must be approved by the group to be valid.
